item.description: The Third Reform Act (1884–1885) The Third Reform Act — consisting of the Franchise Act of 1884 and the Redistribution of Seats Act of 1885 — was the crowning legislative achievement of Gladstone’s second ministry, extending the household suffrage that had been granted to boroughs in 1867 to the cou...

item.title: The Suffragette Movement (1867–1918)
item.description: The Suffragette Movement (1867–1918) The women’s suffrage movement in Britain — encompassing both the constitutional campaign of the National Union of Women’s Suffrage Societies (NUWSS) and the militant direct action of the Women’s Social and Political Union (WSPU) — was one of the most defining soc...

item.title: The Second Reform Act (1867)
item.description: The Second Reform Act (1867) The Reform Act of 1867 — commonly called the Second Reform Act — was the most dramatic volte-face in nineteenth-century British politics.

item.title: The Scramble for Africa and Partition (1880–1914)
item.description: The Scramble for Africa and Partition (1880–1914) The Scramble for Africa was the rapid invasion, occupation, colonisation, and partition of the African continent by European powers during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

item.title: The Great Labour Unrest (1911–1914)
item.description: The Great Labour Unrest (1911–1914) Between 1911 and the outbreak of the Great War, British industrial life was shaken by a wave of strikes and lock-outs on a scale that contemporaries compared to a labour war.

item.title: The Entente Cordiale and the Alliance System (1904–1914)
item.description: The Entente Cordiale and the Alliance System (1904–1914) The Entente Cordiale was the series of diplomatic agreements signed between Britain and France on 8 April 1904 that resolved a century of colonial rivalry and laid the foundation for the Anglo-French alliance that fought the First World War.

item.title: The General Election of 1906 & Tariff Reform
item.description: The General Election of 1906 & Tariff Reform The general election of January–February 1906 produced one of the most decisive Liberal landslides in British electoral history, returning a government with a majority of 134 over all opposition groups combined.

item.title: The Easter Rising (1916)
item.description: The Easter Rising (1916) In the week after Easter 1916 a rising broke out in Dublin that the Annual Register ranked among the outstanding events of the year, with the two Military Service Acts and the later reconstruction of the Government.

item.title: The Boer War (1899–1902)
item.description: The Boer War (1899–1902) The South African War, commonly called the Boer War, was the struggle between the British Empire and the two Dutch republics — the South African Republic (Transvaal) and the Orange Free State — arising from the collision of imperial expansion with Boer resistance.

item.title: The Anglo-German Naval Rivalry (1897–1914)
item.description: The Anglo-German Naval Rivalry (1897–1914) The Anglo-German naval race — the quarter-century struggle between the Royal Navy and the Imperial German Navy for supremacy at sea — was the most consequential armaments competition of the pre-1914 era.
